entities.title: Where Skills/ and Knowledge/ keep their own .dev files
entities.summary: Skills/ and Knowledge/ are copied whole into other repositories, so a .dev folder inside them would travel with them; for now what is recorded about them is in Agents/.dev.
entities.context: populate-dev gives every maintained folder a .dev folder, and the view skills say to write a view in the folder that owns the behavior. But Skills/ and Knowledge/ are copied unchanged to Meta/Agents/Skills/ and Meta/Agents/Knowledge/. A .dev file inside them would carry folder Agents/Skills or Agents/Knowledge into a repository where it lives elsewhere, and validate_knowledge.py there reports a folder that does not match the file's location (and validate_diagrams.py there rejects a view under Knowledge/, whose folder does not exist). In this repository, validate_diagrams.py does not walk Skills/ at all, so a view there would never be checked. So the validators' views and records, and the records about both folders, are kept in Agents/.dev for now.

options.title: Keep them in Agents/.dev
options.consequences: The copies stay unchanged and every file is checked; the records sit one folder above the code they describe.

options.title: Give Skills/ and Knowledge/ their own .dev folders, and leave .dev out when copying
options.consequences: Each record sits beside its code; the installing steps in Skills/README.md and Knowledge/README.md change, and a copy is no longer the folder as it is here. Views in Skills/.dev stay unchecked unless validate_diagrams.py changes.

options.title: Give them their own .dev folders, and have the validators ignore .dev inside Meta/Agents
options.consequences: Copies stay whole and each record sits beside its code; both validators change, and validate_diagrams.py must check its own folder's .dev while still skipping the skills.

origin.description: Raised while giving this repository its own .dev folders.
